facts.fact: Osmosis is flow of solvent through a semipermeable membrane into the solution
facts.quote: the solvent molecules will flow through the membrane from pure solvent to the solution. This process of flow of the solvent is called osmosis.

facts.fact: Water movement from soil into plant roots and up the plant is partly due to osmosis

reason: Osmosis is defined and other examples are carded (mango, saline), but nothing says water moves from soil into roots by osmosis.

facts.fact: Dichloromethane is used as a paint remover
facts.quote: Dichloromethane is widely used as a solvent as a paint remover

facts.fact: Methylene chloride is the common name of dichloromethane

reason: The card says dichloromethane is a paint remover, but no old material links the name methylene chloride to dichloromethane.

facts.fact: Radioactive decay is first order
facts.quote: All natural and artificial radioactive decay of unstable nuclei take place by first order kinetics.

facts.fact: Decomposition of NH3 on hot Pt is zero order (B excluded)
facts.quote: The decomposition of gaseous ammonia on a hot platinum surface is a zero order reaction at high pressure.

facts.fact: Decomposition of N2O5 is first order
Hydrogenation of ethene is first order
facts.quote: Hydrogenation of ethene is an example of first order reaction.

reason: Radioactive decay, ethene hydrogenation and NH3 on platinum are carded, but nothing says N2O5 decomposition is first order.

facts.fact: Mn2+ is oxidised by peroxodisulphate to permanganate (MnO4-)
Peroxodisulphate is reduced to sulphate (SO4 2-)

reason: Old material covers permanganate preparation by fusion of MnO2 and its oxidising reactions, but never the oxidation of Mn2+ by peroxodisulphate.

facts.fact: Titanium(IV) is more stable than Ti(III) or Ti(II)

reason: The old card says Sc and Ti show few oxidation states, but nothing states that Ti(IV) is the most stable.

facts.fact: Dichromate is used for preparing many azo compounds
facts.quote: as an oxidant for preparation of many azo compounds

facts.fact: Dichromate changes to chromate on raising pH, not lowering it (B false)
Dichromate gains 6 electrons in acid, so equivalent weight is M/6 (C false)
facts.quote: Each Cr₂O₇²⁻ is reduced to 2Cr³⁺, which gains 6 electrons.

facts.fact: Cr-O-Cr bond angle is 126 degrees

reason: A, C and D are taught, but the card on pH only says chromate and dichromate interconvert depending on pH, not which way, so statement B cannot be judged.

facts.fact: Spectrochemical order of field strength: F- < C2O4 2- < NH3 < CN-
facts.quote: I– < Br– < SCN – < Cl– < S2– < F – < OH– < C2O42– < H2O < NCS– < edta4– < NH3 < en < CN – < CO

facts.fact: Stronger ligand gives larger crystal field splitting
facts.quote: The spectrochemical series runs from weak to strong field ligands

facts.fact: Larger splitting means higher energy and so shorter wavelength of light absorbed

reason: The ligand order is taught, but no old material turns larger splitting into a shorter wavelength absorbed (the card speaks only of frequency), so the order of wavelengths is not stated.

facts.fact: Gluconic acid: glucose oxidised to a six-carbon carboxylic acid
facts.quote: Glucose gets oxidised to six carbon carboxylic acid (gluconic acid) on reaction with a mild oxidising agent like bromine water.

facts.fact: Saccharic acid is a dicarboxylic acid
facts.quote: glucose as well as gluconic acid both yield a dicarboxylic acid, saccharic acid.

facts.fact: Fructose has a keto group at C2
facts.quote: Fructose also has the molecular formula C6H12O6 and on the basis of its reactions it was found to contain a ketonic functional group at carbon number 2 and six carbons in straight chain as in the case

facts.fact: Tryptophan structure (indole side chain amino acid)

reason: Gluconic acid, saccharic acid and fructose are carded, but tryptophan is never named or drawn, so that pair comes only by elimination.

facts.fact: Use delta G° = -nFE°cell (as a worked bank calculation, not a formula alone)
n = 2 for Ni + 2Ag+ -> Ni2+ + 2Ag
Compute delta G° = -2 x 96487 x 0.80 J = -154.4 kJ/mol

facts.fact: Reimer-Tiemann: phenol + CHCl3 + NaOH puts CHO at ortho
facts.quote: On treating phenol with chloroform in the presence of sodium hydroxide, a –CHO group is introduced at ortho position of benzene ring.

facts.fact: An intermediate substituted benzal chloride is hydrolysed to salicylaldehyde
facts.quote: The intermediate substituted benzal chloride is hydrolysed in the presence of alkali to produce salicylaldehyde.

facts.fact: The intermediate is the sodium phenoxide carrying -CHCl2 at ortho (not the phenol form)

reason: Cards name a substituted benzal chloride intermediate, but nothing shows it as the ortho -CHCl2 phenoxide rather than the phenol form, which is all that separates options 2 and 3.
